newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares soar despite technical glitches.
newsitem.headline: German shares soar despite technical glitches.

text.p: The German share market extended its race higher on Wednesday to end floor trading up 4.15 percent even though trading was temporarily suspended amid technical problems.

Germany's blue-chip DAX index closed floor trade at 4,406.09 points or 175.67 above Tuesday's closing level as the strong dollar and a moderate outlook for inflation continued to fuel the market's wild rally.
In late afternoon electronic trading however profit-taking chipped away at some of the index's gains leaving the IBIS DAX up 2.03 percent at 4,384.82.

U.S. central bank officials, responsible for sending the German market higher this morning, were also credited with laying the ground-work for some of the profit-taking in late afternoon, dealers said.

Trading got off to a very strong start as German markets, including equities and bonds, celebrated U.S. markets' advances overnight triggered by the U.S. Federal Reserve's moderate outlook on inflation.

But a series of technical problems hobbled trading throughout the session, suspending electronic trade downed for periods during the morning and forcing all floor trading a halt in early afternoon. The bourse however extended its trading hours to compensate for lost time.
Bourse sources said Wednesday's problems were linked to a system overload, something which had already plagued bourse trading on Monday.
Throughout the session, the strong U.S. dollar, positive news on results and hopes for more consolidation in the industry pushed German bank shares higher.
"The banks are up, the cars are up. The DTB options guys are starting to buy. Everything is good as gold as far as I can see," a Frankfurt trader said.

Deutsche Bank, the nation's leading commercial bank, reported a stronger-than-expected 27.5 percent rise in group net income in the first half of 1997 and was rewarded with an 5.59 mark rise to 125.50 in its share price in electronic IBIS trading.
Bayerische Vereinsbank, fresh from announcing it would merge with another Bavarian bank, posted an 11.50 mark gain to 111.50 marks.
Similarly German chemical shares remained in vogue with all three of the nation's largest chemical and drugs firms moving higher. Hoechst led the pack with a 2.25 mark gain to 85.45.
